'''''Digitalis mariana''''' is a [[flowering plant]] species in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Plantaginaceae]]. It is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[Digitalis|foxglove]] with [[evergreen]] foliage and rose-red flowers, which are produced in summer.<ref name="Kole2011">{{cite book|last=Kole |first=Chittaranjan |title=Wild Crop Relatives: Genomic and Breeding Resources: Plantation and Ornamental Crops |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UdDMCfgr4dEC&pg=PA78|date=1 September 2011 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-642-21201-7 |pages=78–}}</ref> It is native to [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]].<ref name=PoWO>{{cite web |title=''Digitalis mariana'' Boiss. |date=2017 |work=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/802048-1 |access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref><ref name=EurMed>{{cite web |title=Details for: ''Digitalis purpurea'' subsp. ==Taxonomy==
''Digitalis mariana'' was first [[Species description|described]] as a new species by the Swiss botanist [[Pierre Edmond Boissier]] in 1841.<ref name=ipni/><ref name=Boissier1841>{{cite book |last=Boissier |first=Pierre Edmond |author-link=Pierre Edmond Boissier |date=1841 |title=Voyage botanique dans le midi de l'Espagne |url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/9792/?offset=#page=469 |location=Paris |publisher=Gide et Cie. |page=465–466 |language=fr, la |volume=II }}</ref> Although the ''[[Flora Ibérica]]'' (2009) and the ''[[Plants of the World Online]]'' website (2017) consider it to be a valid, independent species,<ref name=PoWO/><ref name=ibérica/> the ''[[Flora Europaea]]'' (1976)<ref>[http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Digitalis&SPECIES_XREF=&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK=species ''Flora Europaea'', Vol. 4 (1976): ''Digitalis'' species list]</ref> and the ''Euro+Med Plantbase'' (2011) considered it to be two [[subspecies]] of ''[[Digitalis purpurea]]'': subspecies ''mariana'',<ref name=EurMed/> and subspecies ''heywoodii''.<ref name=EurMed2>{{cite web |title=Details for: ''Digitalis purpurea'' subsp. ''heywoodii'' |url=http://ww2.bgbm.org/EuroPlusMed/PTaxonDetail.asp?NameId=33824&PTRefFk=7200000 |last=Marhold |first=Karol |editor-last=Greuter |editor-first=Werner |editor2-last=von Raab-Straube |editor2-first=E. |date=2011 |website=Euro+Med Plantbase |publisher=[[Berlin Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum|Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin-Dahlem]] |access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref>

Two infraspecific [[taxon|taxa]] are accepted:<ref name=PoWO/><ref name=ibérica/><ref>{{cite web |title=Infraspecific Taxon Details : ''Digitalis mariana'' Boiss. |url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/annual-checklist/2019/details/species/id/f57ede25f37dbb1b4047db21051d973c/source/tree |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref>
*''Digitalis mariana'' subsp. ''mariana'' <small>Boiss.</small>
*''Digitalis mariana'' subsp. ''heywoodii'' <small>(Pinto da Silva & Silva) P. A. Hinz</small>

==Description==
The two subspecies can be distinguished by their flower colour and the [[indumentum]] on their [[inflorescence]]. The [[Nominate (taxonomy)|nominate]] form has purple-pink flowers and short glandular hairs of only 0.3–0.4'' ''mm in length, ''heywoodii'' has flowers which are white, or very rarely, yellowish, sometimes with a pinkish line of various shades along the margin of the [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]], and the inflorescence is covered in longish, non-glandular hairs of 2–4'' ''mm.<ref name=ibérica/>

The nominate taxon is locally known in [[Spanish language|Spanish]] as ''campanitas'' or ''dedalera''.<ref name=ANTHOS/><ref name=EurMed/> The Spanish name ''verdolobo'' has been recorded for the subspecies ''heywoodii''.<ref name=ANTHOS/>

===Similar species===
Its native range it closely resembles ''[[Digitalis thapsi]]'', which was also remarked upon by the first botanist to distinguish it as a new species, Boissier.<ref name=Boissier1841/> In the [[Single-access key|dichotomous key]] in the ''Flora Iberica'', it is keyed out to [[Digitalis minor|''D. minor'']], [[Digitalis purpurea|''D. purpurea'']] and ''D. thapsi''.<ref name=ibérica/>

''Digitalis thapsi'' is clearly distinguished by having a very sticky [[indumentum]] formed exclusively of yellowish, glandular hairs which are up to 0.6'' ''mm in length, and having leaves in the middle of the rosette which are clearly [[decurrent]].<ref name=ibérica/>

''Digitalis minor'', an endemic of the [[Balearic Islands]], is not [[sympatric]] to ''D. mariana''. It is distinguished by having the capsule (fruit) clearly shorter than the [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]], a lower lip of the corolla with highly developed lateral lobes which are auricular (ear-like) in shape, clearly split down to the mouth of the tube.<ref name=ibérica/>

''Digitalis purpurea'' is the most similar species, according to the ''Flora Iberica'' key, being separated from ''D. mariana'' by having a calyx with the [[sepal]]s ordinarily more-or-less recurved towards the corolla, sometimes arranged [[Glossary of botanical terms#patent|patently]], and the corolla tube gradually tightening towards its base.<ref name=ibérica/>

In ''D. mariana'' the calyx has sepals which are patent or subpatent and the corolla tube abruptly tightens towards its base, distinguishing it from ''D. purpurea''. The capsule is equal or larger in length than the calyx, and the lower lip of the corolla has lateral lobes which are little developed, rounded, not auricular, nor split to the mouth of the tube, which distinguishes both these species from ''D. minor''. All three species are distinguished from ''D. thapsi'' by the indumentum lacking the long, yellowish, glandular hairs, being less sticky, and instead having silvery or greyish hairs, not all hairs being glandular -or when they are, these are all [[Sessile (botany)|subsessile]].<ref name=ibérica/>

==Distribution==
Both subspecies are primarily found in the [[Sierra Morena]] mountain ranges of the southern [[Iberian Peninsula]], which extend from [[Portugal]] to [[Spain]]. The nominate subspecies is more predominant in the east, the other to the west.<ref name=ibérica/>

The subspecies ''heywoodii'' has been recorded in [[Alto Alentejo Province|Alto Alentejo]] in Portugal, and in Spain in the provinces of [[Province of Badajoz|Badajoz]], [[Province of Cáceres|Cáceres]], [[Province of Córdoba (Spain)|Córdoba]] and [[province of Ciudad Real|Ciudad Real]].<ref name=ibérica/> In [[Andalucía]] it is found in the northeast(???) of the region, on the southern flanks of the Sierra Morena, where it is uncommon.<ref name=Andalucía>{{cite book |last=Cabezudo |first=B. |last2=Talavera |first2=S. |last3=Blanca |first3=G. |last4=Salazar |first4=C. |last5=Cueto |first5=M. The nominate taxon has been found in Badajoz, Córdoba, Ciudad Real, [[Province of Jaén (Spain)|Jaén]] and [[Seville (province)|Sevilla]], and perhaps also [[province of Huelva|Huelva]].<ref name=ibérica/> In Andalucía it is found in the northeast, on the southern flanks of the Sierra Morena, where it is uncommon.<ref name=Andalucía/>

==Ecology==
Both subspecies grow in cracks in the stone in rocky areas. The subspecies ''heywoodii'' is most often found in fissures in [[granite]]<ref name=ibérica/><ref name=Andalucía/> and [[slate]].<ref name=Andalucía/> The nominate subspecies is usually found in more acidic soils, and often in rock falls, loose scree or among boulders.<ref name=ibérica/><ref name=Andalucía/>

The specific [[phytosociology|phytosociological]] [[Association (ecology)|suballiance]] and alliance wherein both subspecies occur is called 'Rumici indurati-Dianthion lusitani', which is in the order 'Phagnalo saxatilis-Rumicetalia indurati', in the class 'Phagnalo saxatilis-Rumicetea indurati'. It is a characteristic species of this phytocoenosis. In this [[habitat]] it occurs together with these following characteristic species: [[Antirrhinum graniticum|''Antirrhinum graniticum'' subsp. ==Conservation==
Both forms are legally protected in [[Extremadura]], where they have the status of a 'taxon of special interest'. ''Digitalis heywoodii'' was listed as 'not threatened' in a 1984 national list of rare or endemic plants of Spain, but in 2000 it was listed as '[[Vulnerable species|vulnerable]]' in the {{Lang|es|Lista roja de la flora vascular Española}}.<ref name=ANTHOS/> Both subspecies were included as 'vulnerable' in the [[Regional Red List]] of Andalucía of 2005.<ref name=ANTHOS/><ref name=Andalucía/> The reason for this was that the different collection localities and populations in this region were small.<ref name=Andalucía/>
